questions.title: Aldosterone decreases sodium excretion
questions.subject: renal
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Renal Physiology > Sodium Regulation
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary physiological function of the hormone aldosterone?

options.D: Markedly increased total body water elimination

explanations.A: Incorrect. Aldosterone promotes potassium secretion (excretion), not potassium reabsorption; it is sodium that is actively reabsorbed under aldosterone's action.
explanations.B: Correct. Aldosterone acts on the distal nephron to increase sodium reabsorption from the tubular fluid back into the blood, so less sodium is lost in the urine — it decreases sodium excretion — while water follows sodium osmotically to expand extracellular fluid volume. The same channels aldosterone upregulates for sodium reabsorption are coupled to potassium secretion, which is why aldosterone excess also causes hypokalemia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aldosterone increases, not decreases, potassium excretion, because the same channels it upregulates for sodium reabsorption are coupled to potassium secretion into the tubular fluid.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Aldosterone promotes water retention (alongside sodium), not water elimination, since water passively follows the reabsorbed sodium.

questions.learning_objective: State that aldosterone decreases urinary sodium excretion by increasing sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron, with a coupled increase in potassium secretion.
